subject: physics_2
question_text: How do you convert a moving coil galvanometer into a voltmeter?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: a high resistance in series with the galvanometer limits the coil current to its small full-scale value for a large applied potential difference, and gives the combination the high overall resistance a voltmeter must have. Matches the book's answer.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The mirror of the ammeter conversion: HIGH resistance, in SERIES — students who swap the two lose both conversion questions at once.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Connect a high resistance in series
lines: A moving coil galvanometer is converted
into a voltmeter by connecting a high
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both words matter: HIGH resistance, in SERIES.
steps.why: In series, the same small current passes through the added resistance and the coil, so a large applied potential difference still drives only the coil's safe current.
common_mistakes: Saying a low resistance is connected. A low resistance in parallel makes an ammeter, not a voltmeter.
Saying the resistance is in parallel. In parallel it would not limit the coil current.

recall.must_convey: That a high resistance is connected in series with the galvanometer.

steps.memory_tip: Voltmeter needs a brake in the line: a high resistance in series.

steps.label: Why the series resistance works
lines: The high resistance limits the current
through the coil to its small full-scale
value even when a large potential
difference is applied across the meter.
The combination also has a high overall
resistance, so it draws very little
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two effects: the coil is protected, and the meter as a whole draws almost no current.
steps.why: A voltmeter must read the potential difference between two points without disturbing the circuit, so its total resistance has to be high — the series resistance provides exactly that.
common_mistakes: Saying the series resistance increases the current. It reduces the coil current for a given potential difference.
Forgetting that the high total resistance is what stops the meter loading the circuit.

recall.must_convey: That the series resistance limits the coil current and gives the meter a high total resistance.
accept: limits the current through the coil
reject: most current goes through the shunt

steps.memory_tip: Series brake: big voltage outside, same small current inside the coil.
